regime_context: China A-shares thematic tape is narrow and two-headed: Banks (eligibility gate says in-trend, broad, high durability) and Innovative Pharma/CXO sit almost tied at the top, both crowded. The rotation radar shows a near-zero leader margin, only 18% of themes eligible, and no directional handoff — leadership is contested, not settled. The trend gate did NOT hold on this market's history (mean-reverting tape), so the one validated edge is absent here; the track record adds further humility (directional accuracy 0.38 on 77 calls).
emerging_watch: Watching whether Innovative Pharma & CXO (159992.SZ) closes the rotation gap on Banks (512800.SS) and widens it beyond a 0.05 leader-margin advantage while keeping its eligibility flag — that combination would retire this watch and point to a confirmed handoff.

theses.subject: Banks
theses.thesis: Banks are the only top-ranked theme that clears the absolute-trend gate (eligible=true), with broad participation (breadth 0.89) and high durability (0.73). This is a trend-following lean, not a momentum call — the gate is the discipline leg, and it happens to be the one leg whose absence (gate_helps=false) has already been flagged as a reason to stay humble here. Crowding_z 1.78 is a size-down caution only: do not chase, but also do not fade the leader.
evidence: eligible=true with durability_bar 0.73 (highest among eligible themes)
breadth 0.889 — the only theme with broad, cohesive participation
theses.dissent: The gate_helps=false verdict means the trend discipline whipsawed on this mean-reverting market before — the eligibility flag may be exactly the kind of signal that fails here. Banks at crowding_z 1.78 are the most crowded theme, and crowding on the leader has historically marked tops, not entries.

falsifier.text: 512800.SS trails the CSI 300 benchmark by 5% or more before the check-by date (2026-10-28).

theses.subject: Innovative Pharma & CXO
theses.thesis: Pharma/CXO is within 0.01 of the leader in rotation score and is the only credible challenger, but its trend leg is weaker (breadth 0.64, durability 0.60) and it is also crowded (z 1.59). The lean is expressed as a conditional: it is the one theme positioned to CONFIRM a handoff if Banks stall. It is a size-capped overweight, not a conviction buy, and explicitly not a prediction of leadership change.
evidence: rotation challenger with margin of only 0.01 vs Banks
theses.dissent: Two crowded themes at the top with nearly identical scores means the tape has not chosen a leader. Pharma's lower breadth (0.643) and durability (0.60) suggest the flow is narrower and less cohesive than Banks — if money rotates, Pharma may simply be the runner-up that fades rather than the handoff that wins.

falsifier.text: 159992.SZ lags 512800.SS by 5% or more over the next 20 trading days without Banks giving up its eligibility flag.

theses.subject: Anticipate a contested-leadership sideways chop in the top two
theses.thesis: The rotation radar explicitly shows a non-directional, contested structure: leader margin 0.01, one_narrative=false, directional=false, absorption 0.32, and only 4 of 22 themes eligible (18%). With the validated gate edge absent on this market and directional accuracy at 0.38, the most honest lean on the broad tape is to avoid committing to either top theme as a decisive winner in the near term. This 'avoid' applies to the structural ambiguity, not to specific scorable themes.
evidence: gate_helps=false — the discipline did not hold here
theses.dissent: A contested leader reading can understate persistence: Banks has held the top rank with high breadth and durability, which may simply be a stable, if narrow, value regime rather than an unresolved choppy one.

falsifier.text: The rotation radar shows a confirmed handoff (leader margin widens to 0.05 or more, or directional flips to true) before the check-by date.

check.reason: theme has no scalar etf_proxy → not cleanly scorable

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
